question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is responsible for DNA replication?
explanation: The S phase (Synthesis phase) is the stage where DNA replication occurs, doubling the genetic material.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: What distinguishes anaphase I of meiosis from anaphase of mitosis?

options.text:
(1)
Sister chromatids separate in meiosis but not in mitosis

(2)
Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis but not in mitosis

(3)
DNA replication occurs in anaphase I

(4)
Centromeres do not split in mitosis

explanation:
In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate, whereas in mitosis, sister chromatids
              separate.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following events occurs during anaphase I of meiosis?
explanation: In anaphase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number by half.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements about anaphase is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements about cytokinesis is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Animal cells form a cleavage furrow

(2)
Plant cells divide by forming a cleavage furrow

(4)
Cytokinesis does not occur in mitosis

explanation:
In animal cells, cytokinesis occurs by forming a cleavage furrow, while in plant cells, a cell plate
              forms instead.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following events occurs in anaphase?

options.text:
(1)
Chromosomes align at the center of the cell

(2)
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles of the cell.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which phase of mitosis directly follows metaphase?
explanation: Anaphase follows metaphase, during which sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which checkpoint ensures proper chromosome alignment before anaphase begins?
explanation:
The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly aligned at the metaphase plate before anaphase
              begins.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: What is the outcome of meiosis II?
explanation:
Meiosis II results in four haploid daughter cells, each with half the chromosome number of the parent
              cell.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following happens during pachytene of meiosis I?
explanation: During pachytene, homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material through crossing over.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 1

question_text: Which structure is responsible for chromosome movement during cell division?
explanation:
Spindle fibers, composed of microtubules, attach to kinetochores on chromosomes and facilitate their
              movement.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which phase of interphase is characterized by intense metabolic activity and cell growth?
explanation:
The G1 phase is the period between mitosis and DNA replication, characterized by active metabolism and
              cell growth.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is correct?

options.text:
(1)
It occurs only in haploid cells

(2)
It results in genetically identical daughter cells

(3)
It reduces the chromosome number by half

(4)
It occurs only in reproductive cells

explanation:
Mitosis produces two genetically identical daughter cells, maintaining the chromosome number of the
              parent cell.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about G0 phase is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Cells in G0 phase cannot divide again

(2)
Cells in G0 phase are metabolically inactive

(3)
Cells in G0 phase can re-enter the cell cycle under specific conditions

(4)
G0 phase is a part of mitosis

explanation: Cells in G0 phase are metabolically active and can re-enter the cell cycle when needed.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about the G1 phase is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
It is the first phase of interphase

(2)
Cell growth and metabolism occur in this phase

(3)
DNA replication occurs in this phase

explanation: DNA replication does not occur in G1; it takes place in the S phase.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Mitosis occurs in both somatic and germ cells

(2)
Mitosis produces two diploid daughter cells

explanation: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase is correct?
explanation: During telophase, the nuclear membrane reforms around each set of chromosomes, which decondense.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following phases is also known as the “resting phase” of the cell cycle?
explanation: The G0 phase is a quiescent phase where cells temporarily or permanently exit the cell cycle.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which structure helps separate chromosomes during mitosis?
explanation: Spindle fibers attach to chromosomes via kinetochores and help pull them apart during mitosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases

(2)
Mitosis is the longest phase of the cell cycle

(3)
DNA replication occurs in the G2 phase

(4)
Cell division does not occur in prokaryotes

explanation:
Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases, where the cell prepares for division. Mitosis is not the
              longest phase, and DNA replication occurs in the S phase.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 2

question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is known as the "resting phase"?
explanation: The G0 phase is a quiescent stage where cells do not divide but remain metabolically active.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about the quiescent phase (G0) is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Cells in G0 never re-enter the cell cycle

(2)
G0 phase is a metabolically inactive state

(3)
Cells can re-enter the cell cycle when required

(4)
G0 phase is the shortest phase in the cell cycle

explanation:
Cells in G0 remain metabolically active and can re-enter the cell cycle when stimulated by external
              signals.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following occurs during telophase I of meiosis?
explanation: During telophase I, homologous chromosomes reach opposite poles, and nuclear membranes may reappear.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: What is the function of the centrioles during mitosis?
explanation: Centrioles help in forming spindle fibers that assist in the movement of chromosomes during mitosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about diplotene is correct?
explanation:
During diplotene, chiasmata (points of crossing over) become visible as homologous chromosomes start
              separating.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Meiosis II reduces the chromosome number

(2)
Meiosis II involves separation of homologous chromosomes

(4)
Meiosis II produces diploid daughter cells

explanation:
Meiosis II is similar to mitosis in that sister chromatids separate, but it does not reduce the
              chromosome number further.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about cytokinesis?

options.text:
(2)
Animal cells undergo cytokinesis by forming a cell plate

(3)
Cytokinesis ensures equal distribution of cytoplasm

(4)
Cytokinesis differs between plant and animal cells

explanation: Animal cells divide by forming a cleavage furrow, whereas plant cells form a cell plate.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following phases is the longest in the cell cycle?
explanation: G1 phase is the longest phase of the cell cycle, where cells grow and prepare for DNA replication.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following is NOT a function of mitosis?

options.text:
(2)
Repair and replacement of damaged cells

explanation:
Gamete formation occurs through meiosis, not mitosis. Mitosis is responsible for growth, repair, and
              asexual reproduction.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase of mitosis?

options.text:
(4)
Chromosomes are aligned at the equator

explanation:
During prophase, chromosomes condense, the nuclear membrane breaks down, and spindle fibers form, but
              chromosome alignment occurs in metaphase.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 3

question_text: Which phase of the cell cycle is the longest in a typical eukaryotic cell?
explanation: Interphase occupies more than 95% of the cell cycle and includes G1, S, and G2 phases.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: What is the significance of meiosis in sexually reproducing organisms?

options.text:
(1)
It reduces the chromosome number to half, ensuring genetic diversity

(2)
It produces identical cells for growth and repair

(4)
It only helps in asexual reproduction

explanation:
Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half and ensures genetic variation in sexually reproducing
              organisms.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following events occurs during prophase I of meiosis but not in prophase of mitosis?
explanation:
Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis, leading to genetic recombination, whereas it does not
              occur in mitosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following best describes the metaphase plate?

options.text:
(2)
Region where spindle fibers are synthesized

(3)
Plane where chromosomes align during metaphase

(4)
Structure that holds sister chromatids together

explanation:
During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, an imaginary plane equidistant from the
              spindle poles.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: What happens during the diplotene stage of prophase I?

options.text:
(4)
Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

explanation:
During diplotene, homologous chromosomes start separating as the synaptonemal complex dissolves, but
              remain attached at chiasmata.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following is true about anaphase I of meiosis?

options.text:
(2)
Homologous chromosomes move to opposite poles

explanation: In anaphase I, homologous chromosomes (not sister chromatids) separate and move to opposite poles.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following statements about the cell cycle is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle

(2)
M phase includes mitosis and cytokinesis

(3)
G1 phase occurs after the S phase

(4)
S phase is responsible for DNA replication

explanation: G1 phase occurs before the S phase, not after it.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following statements about interphase is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Interphase consists of G1, S, and G2 phases

(2)
Interphase is the shortest phase of the cell cycle

(3)
DNA replication occurs in the S phase of interphase

(4)
Interphase prepares the cell for mitosis

explanation: Interphase is the longest phase of the cell cycle, not the shortest.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about the G1 phase?

options.text:
(1)
The cell grows in size during G1 phase

(2)
Organelles are duplicated in G1 phase

(3)
DNA replication occurs in G1 phase

(4)
Cells prepare for DNA synthesis in G1 phase

explanation: DNA replication does not occur in G1 phase; it happens in the S phase.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following is correct about the M checkpoint?

options.text:
(1)
It ensures that DNA replication is complete

(2)
It occurs at the end of G1 phase

(3)
It ensures that all chromosomes are attached to spindle fibers before anaphase

explanation:
The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly attached to spindle fibers before anaphase
              begins.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following is correct about anaphase?

options.text:
(1)
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

(2)
Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and are pulled toward opposite poles by spindle fibers.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which phase of mitosis immediately follows metaphase?
explanation: Anaphase follows metaphase, where sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase is incorrect?
explanation: During telophase, sister chromatids have already separated in anaphase; they do not remain attached.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following is true about the S phase of interphase?

options.text:
(1)
DNA replication occurs, doubling the chromosome number

(2)
The cell grows and prepares for mitosis

explanation:
During the S phase, DNA is replicated, doubling the chromosome content of the cell but not the chromosome
              number.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following is an example of a cell type that remains in the G0 phase permanently?
explanation: Nerve cells enter G0 phase permanently and do not divide after differentiation.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Meiosis II reduces the chromosome number

(2)
Meiosis II involves separation of homologous chromosomes

(4)
Meiosis II produces diploid daughter cells

explanation:
Meiosis II is similar to mitosis in that sister chromatids separate, but it does not reduce the
              chromosome number further.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about the quiescent (G0) phase is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Cells in G0 phase are metabolically inactive

(2)
Nerve and heart cells enter G0 permanently

(3)
Cells in G0 phase cannot re-enter the cell cycle

(4)
G0 phase occurs after mitosis and before cytokinesis

explanation:
Nerve and heart cells remain in G0 permanently, while some other cells may re-enter the cycle under
              specific conditions.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following structures plays a crucial role in cytokinesis of plant cells?
explanation:
In plant cells, cytokinesis occurs via the formation of a cell plate, which eventually develops into a
              new cell wall.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about the centromere?

options.text:
(1)
It is the region where sister chromatids are attached

(2)
Spindle fibers attach to the centromere during cell division

(3)
It helps in the separation of homologous chromosomes in meiosis

explanation: The centromere remains intact during metaphase and serves as the attachment site for spindle fibers.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about interphase is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Interphase is also called the resting phase

(2)
DNA replication occurs in the S phase of interphase

(3)
G1 phase follows the S phase

(4)
G2 phase prepares the cell for mitosis

explanation: G1 phase comes before the S phase, not after it.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following occurs at the end of meiosis?
explanation: Meiosis results in the formation of four genetically distinct haploid cells.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: During which phase of mitosis does chromatin condense into visible chromosomes?
explanation: During prophase, chromatin condenses into distinct chromosomes, making them visible under a microscope.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Meiosis results in four haploid cells

(3)
Meiosis is a type of asexual reproduction

explanation: Meiosis is a type of sexual reproduction, not asexual reproduction.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: What is the role of kinetochores during cell division?

options.text:
(1)
Act as sites of spindle fiber attachment

explanation: Kinetochores are protein structures on the centromere where spindle fibers attach to move chromosomes.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: What is the primary purpose of meiosis II?

options.text:
(2)
To reduce chromosome number by half

explanation:
Meiosis II is similar to mitosis and is responsible for the separation of sister chromatids into
              different cells.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: How does meiosis contribute to genetic variation?

options.text:
(1)
By ensuring identical copies of DNA are passed to daughter cells

(2)
Through crossing over and independent assortment

(4)
Through DNA replication in meiosis II

explanation:
Meiosis introduces genetic variation through crossing over during prophase I and independent assortment
              during metaphase I.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: What is the role of kinetochores during cell division?

options.text:
(2)
They help in chromosome movement by attaching to spindle fibers

explanation:
Kinetochores are protein structures at the centromere that facilitate chromosome movement by attaching to
              spindle fibers.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of telophase in mitosis?
explanation:
Centromeres divide in anaphase, not telophase. In telophase, chromosomes decondense and the nuclear
              membrane reforms.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about metaphase I of meiosis?

options.text:
(1)
Homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

explanation:
In metaphase I, homologous chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, but sister chromatids remain
              together.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about chromatin and chromosomes is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Chromatin is the condensed form of chromosomes

(2)
Chromosomes exist only during cell division

(3)
Chromatin is composed of DNA and proteins

explanation:
Chromatin consists of DNA and proteins (mainly histones) and condenses into chromosomes during cell
              division.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 6

question_text: At which stage of mitosis do chromosomes align at the center of the cell?
explanation:
During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, preparing for equal distribution to daughter
              cells.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase is correct?

options.text:
(3)
Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

explanation: During telophase, the nuclear membrane reforms around the separated chromosomes.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: Which phase of meiosis is responsible for the formation of chiasmata?
explanation:
During diplotene, homologous chromosomes begin to separate except at chiasmata, where crossing over has
              occurred.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: What is the function of recombinase enzyme in meiosis?
explanation:
Recombinase is an enzyme that facilitates crossing over during the pachytene stage of prophase I in
              meiosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following statements about cell division checkpoints is correct?

options.text:
(1)
G1 checkpoint ensures DNA has replicated correctly

(2)
M checkpoint ensures chromosomes are aligned properly

(3)
G2 checkpoint occurs before DNA replication

explanation: The M checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly aligned before proceeding to anaphase.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis II is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Meiosis II is identical to mitosis

(2)
Meiosis II reduces the chromosome number

(3)
DNA replication occurs before meiosis II

(4)
Meiosis II produces diploid daughter cells

explanation:
Meiosis II is similar to mitosis, as it involves the separation of sister chromatids without further
              reduction in chromosome number.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: Which structure disappears during prophase of mitosis?
explanation: During prophase, the nuclear envelope disintegrates, allowing spindle fibers to attach to chromosomes.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: What is the end result of meiosis in terms of chromosome number?
explanation:
Meiosis results in haploid cells, ensuring that gametes have half the chromosome number of the parent
              cell.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase I of meiosis?

options.text:
(1)
It is longer and more complex than prophase of mitosis

explanation: Crossing over occurs in the pachytene stage, not in zygotene.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: What is a key difference between meiosis I and meiosis II?

options.text:
(1)
DNA replication occurs in meiosis I but not in meiosis II

(2)
Homologous chromosomes separate in meiosis II, not in meiosis I

(3)
Meiosis I produces haploid cells, while meiosis II produces diploid cells

(4)
Cytokinesis occurs only in meiosis I

explanation:
DNA replication occurs only in meiosis I during the S phase, not in meiosis II, which is similar to
              mitosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 7

question_text: Which event is unique to meiosis and does not occur in mitosis?
explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I of meiosis and is responsible for genetic recombination.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: What is the primary function of the centromere during cell division?
explanation:
The centromere serves as the attachment site for spindle fibers, ensuring proper chromosome movement
              during division.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which type of cell division occurs in the apical and lateral meristem of plants?
explanation: Mitosis occurs in the apical and lateral meristem, leading to the continuous growth of plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about meiosis is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Meiosis occurs in both diploid and haploid cells

(2)
Meiosis involves two rounds of cell division

(3)
Meiosis results in the production of diploid cells

(4)
Meiosis does not contribute to genetic variation

explanation:
Meiosis consists of two divisions (meiosis I and II) and produces haploid cells, contributing to genetic
              variation.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which event marks the transition from prophase to metaphase in mitosis?
explanation:
The complete disintegration of the nuclear envelope marks the transition from prophase to metaphase in
              mitosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about prophase is incorrect?
explanation:
During prophase, the nuclear envelope breaks down, allowing the spindle fibers to interact with
              chromosomes.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following is correct about G2 phase?

options.text:
(1)
G2 phase occurs before the S phase

(2)
The cell checks for DNA replication errors in G2 phase

(3)
G2 phase is longer than G1 phase

(4)
DNA replication takes place in G2 phase

explanation:
The G2 phase is a checkpoint where the cell ensures that DNA replication was completed correctly before
              mitosis begins.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about metaphase is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

(3)
Sister chromatids move to opposite poles

(4)
Metaphase is the best stage to study chromosome morphology

explanation:
During metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate, but sister chromatids move to opposite poles
              in anaphase.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: During which phase of mitosis do spindle fibers attach to kinetochores?
explanation:
During metaphase, spindle fibers attach to kinetochores and align the chromosomes at the equatorial
              plate.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about genetic variation in meiosis?

options.text:
(1)
Crossing over occurs during prophase I

(2)
Independent assortment occurs during metaphase I

(3)
Meiosis results in genetically identical cells

explanation:
Meiosis produces genetically varied cells due to crossing over and independent assortment, not identical
              ones.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis?

options.text:
(2)
Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half

(3)
Meiosis consists of one round of division

explanation: Meiosis consists of two rounds of division (meiosis I and meiosis II), not just one.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase II of meiosis?
explanation: In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate, similar to anaphase of mitosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about mitosis is incorrect?

options.text:
(2)
Mitosis results in two genetically identical daughter cells

(4)
Mitosis is essential for growth and repair

explanation: Crossing over does not occur in mitosis; it occurs during prophase I of meiosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about G2 phase?

options.text:
(2)
Proteins necessary for mitosis are synthesized

(3)
DNA replication occurs in this phase

explanation: DNA replication occurs in the S phase, not in G2.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about metaphase?

options.text:
(1)
Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate

(4)
Metaphase is an important stage for karyotyping

explanation: Sister chromatids do not separate in metaphase; they separate during anaphase.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: Which event distinguishes meiosis I from mitosis?

options.text:
(3)
Homologous chromosomes pair and undergo recombination

explanation:
During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes pair up and undergo recombination, which does not occur in
              mitosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: Which phase of meiosis involves the separation of sister chromatids?
explanation: During anaphase II, the sister chromatids of each chromosome separate and move toward opposite poles.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about prophase I of meiosis?

options.text:
(1)
It is longer than prophase of mitosis

(4)
Chromosomes do not condense in prophase I

explanation: Chromosomes condense during prophase I of meiosis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: What is the main feature of metaphase I of meiosis?

options.text:
(1)
Chromosomes align at the equator as bivalents

(2)
Chromatids separate and move to opposite poles

explanation: In metaphase I, bivalents (paired homologous chromosomes) align at the metaphase plate.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: What is the function of spindle fibers during cell division?
explanation:
Spindle fibers attach to kinetochores and help in the movement and separation of chromatids or homologous
              chromosomes during cell division.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 9

question_text: What happens to the chromosome number during meiosis I?
explanation:
During meiosis I, homologous chromosomes separate, reducing the chromosome number from diploid to
              haploid.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following occurs during anaphase I but not in mitotic anaphase?
explanation:
During anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate, whereas in mitotic anaphase, sister chromatids
              separate.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about prophase is correct?
explanation: During prophase, centrosomes migrate to opposite poles to form the mitotic spindle.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which event occurs in anaphase II but not in anaphase I?
explanation: In anaphase II, sister chromatids separate, whereas in anaphase I, homologous chromosomes separate.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about crossing over in meiosis?

options.text:
(1)
Crossing over occurs during pachytene of prophase I

(2)
It involves exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes

(3)
Crossing over leads to genetic recombination

(4)
Crossing over occurs during metaphase II

explanation: Crossing over occurs during pachytene of prophase I, not in metaphase II.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about meiosis?

options.text:
(2)
Meiosis reduces the chromosome number by half

(3)
Meiosis consists of one round of division

explanation: Meiosis consists of two rounds of division (meiosis I and meiosis II), not just one.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about telophase I of meiosis is incorrect?

options.text:
(3)
DNA replication occurs before meiosis II

explanation: There is no DNA replication between meiosis I and II.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?

options.text:
(1)
Mitosis produces haploid cells, meiosis produces diploid cells

(2)
Mitosis occurs in gametes, meiosis occurs in somatic cells

(3)
Mitosis produces identical cells, meiosis results in genetic variation

(4)
Mitosis involves two cell divisions, meiosis involves one

explanation:
Mitosis produces genetically identical cells, while meiosis introduces genetic variation through
              recombination.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which stage of mitosis is best for studying chromosome morphology?
explanation:
In metaphase, chromosomes are fully condensed and aligned at the equatorial plate, making them ideal for
              studying morphology.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following is incorrect about the G0 phase?

options.text:
(1)
G0 is a resting phase where cells do not divide

(2)
Nerve and muscle cells remain in G0 permanently

(3)
All cells in G0 phase can never re-enter the cell cycle

(4)
G0 phase occurs after the G1 phase

explanation: Some cells in G0 can re-enter the cell cycle under specific conditions.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Cell Cycle and Cell Division / Test 10
